newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lower fruit, vege prices drive Dec fall in NZ FPI.
newsitem.headline: Lower fruit, vege prices drive Dec fall in NZ FPI.

text.p: Lower prices of fruit, vegetables and groceries were the main contributors to the fall in New Zealand's Food Price Index in December, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
The index fell 0.7 percent in December, following a fall of 0.1 percent in November and a rise of 0.4 percent in October. It is now 1.7 percent higher than in December 1995.

Food and vegetable prices fell 3.0 percent in December, largely due to lower prices for cauliflower, lettuce and tomatoes. General fruit and vegetable prices are now 4.2 percent lower than a year ago.
Grocery prices fell 0.5 percent in December, with lower prices of potato crisps, snack foods, bread and coffee behind the general grocery price decrease.
SNZ said Christmas specials contributed to the December fall in grocery prices, which was the first fall since June 1996.

Meat, fish and poultry prices fell 0.4 percent in December, due largely to lower prices of lamb roasts and steak. The fall was partly offset, however, by a rise in the price of fresh and frozen poultry.

Restaurant meals and ready-to-eat food was the only group to record an increase, up two percent from December 1995. The price of restaurant meals was unchanged in December, but ready-to-eat food prices rose 0.1 percent.
The South Island recorded a food price fall of 1.0 percent in December, while the North Island recorded a fall of 0.6 percent. -- Wellington newsroom (64 4) 473 4746
